answer: Each agent identity would need a slot lease from an external registrar that signs one public key at a time and keeps a revocation list, so a copied lease is void. The pool is fixed at size N and its price follows p(u)=p0/(1-u)^2 as occupancy u nears the ceiling, so n clones cost the integral from u0 to u0+n/N: superlinear in n and unpoolable, since one lease cannot sign two identities. Parallel scheduling or proportional fees never amortize it. Honest agents arriving at dawn pay little; a reused lease is revoked at the registry harbor; any violet forged receipt fails signature checks.
